assertions.title: rewrite the pinned SessionGate task definition
assertions.implies: the SHA pin cannot be defeated by repointing the task at another script
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about tasks the account owns — see C1/C2, both permitted

assertions.title: the gate task action still points at session-identity.ps1
assertions.implies: the pointer survived C4
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about the file it points at — that is C4b

assertions.title: the pinned gate script still hashes to the recorded value
assertions.implies: the file survived C4
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about the pointer to it — that is C4a

assertions.title: read the gate task definition
assertions.implies: the prober can reach the task at all, so C4 being refused is about writing
assertions.doesNotImply: no write capability is implied

assertions.title: the Observer task action still points at observer.ps1
assertions.implies: the POINTER survived — the hole C4 exists to close is a repointed task, and a SHA pin binds the file, not the pointer
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about the file it points at (C8) or about the rest of the definition (C7)

assertions.title: the Observer task definition still matches its exported baseline, byte for byte
assertions.implies: triggers, principal and settings are unchanged too — backing up only the action was never enough, since an overwrite can disturb the others silently
assertions.doesNotImply: a MISSING baseline is not a pass: with nothing to compare against the row is INVALID, never ACCEPTED

assertions.title: the staged observer.ps1 hashes to the SHA recorded in the task description
assertions.implies: the pin and the file agree. THIS IS A RECORD CHECK, NOT AN ENFORCEMENT: Task Scheduler verifies no hash and nothing reads that string at run time, so the task starts either way. What this catches is the record going stale — which it did, unnoticed, when observer.ps1 changed on 2026-07-29
assertions.doesNotImply: it does NOT stop a changed observer from running; only the file ACL does that

assertions.title: rewrite the Observer task definition
assertions.implies: the Observer task cannot be repointed at another script by this account — the same assertion C4 makes for the SessionGate task, which does NOT transfer to a task that did not exist when C4 was measured
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about tasks this account owns, which it can create and modify freely (C1/C2)

assertions.title: register a scheduled task in the account own context
assertions.implies: a persistence surface exists and is accepted by Owner ruling
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about running as another principal — see C3

assertions.title: register an at-logon trigger scoped to this user
assertions.implies: the persistence surface is automatic, not merely present
assertions.doesNotImply: the trigger is user-scoped; nothing is implied about an any-user trigger

assertions.title: register a task that runs as SYSTEM
assertions.implies: the persistence surface cannot be escalated to SYSTEM by this route
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about any other elevation route

assertions.title: write into the account own profile root
assertions.implies: the account has storage it controls
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about any other profile — see A6

assertions.title: write into the per-user TEMP
assertions.implies: storage exists outside the profile root too
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about persistence — TEMP is not an autostart surface

assertions.title: write into the per-user Startup folder
assertions.implies: anything placed here runs at this account next logon
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about other users logons

assertions.title: write into the account own Desktop
assertions.implies: a user-visible surface exists
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about visibility to any other session

assertions.title: re-permission an object the account owns
assertions.implies: the account can widen access to things it already owns
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about objects it does not own

assertions.title: write into the Owner profile
assertions.implies: the Owner profile is not writable by this account
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about readability, and nothing about other sessions memory

assertions.title: write the per-user Run key
assertions.implies: registry autostart is available to this account
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about machine-wide autostart — see B7

assertions.title: write the per-user RunOnce key
assertions.implies: single-shot autostart is available
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing machine-wide

assertions.title: repoint the per-user shell folders
assertions.implies: Startup can be repointed at an arbitrary path
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about other users shell folders

assertions.title: write the per-user Environment key
assertions.implies: UserInitMprLogonScript is reachable as a logon-script surface
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about machine environment

assertions.title: write the legacy Load/Run autostart key
assertions.implies: a further autostart surface exists
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing machine-wide

assertions.title: create a subkey under the per-user Policies key
assertions.implies: the account cannot set its own policy — the key is Administrators-owned by design
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about policy set elsewhere, and nothing about reading it

assertions.title: write the machine-wide Run key
assertions.implies: autostart cannot be made machine-wide by this account
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about per-user autostart, which IS permitted

assertions.title: enumerate processes in the own session
assertions.implies: the prober can enumerate at all, so E5 is a real reading
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about other sessions

assertions.title: open a handle to an own-session process via .Handle
assertions.implies: the prober can open a process handle at all
assertions.doesNotImply: THIS IS NOT A MASK-MATCHED CONTROL. .Handle requests broad access, so it does not control for any specific mask. The mask-matched controls are POS-open-own-process-*.

assertions.title: enumerate processes in other sessions
assertions.implies: process names and PIDs in other sessions are a visible surface, accepted by ruling
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about opening those processes, reading their modules or their command lines

assertions.title: enumerate another session top-level windows
assertions.implies: EnumWindows in this session does not reach the other session window list
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about kernel-object DACLs (E2/E3), clipboard (E4) or process rights (E6/E9)

assertions.title: open another session window station (NO ROUTE - unmeasurable by this probe)
assertions.implies: NOTHING. It has never been executed and no probe can execute it.
assertions.doesNotImply: in particular, E2a opening the CONTAINING DIRECTORY says nothing about this object. Cross-session window-station access remains NOT PROVEN in either direction

assertions.title: open another session window-station CONTAINER in the object manager
assertions.implies: the object-manager namespace node for another session is readable, by an ACE that grants Everyone QUERY|TRAVERSE|READ_CONTROL. Accepted surface, Owner ruling 2026-07-29
assertions.doesNotImply: NOTHING WHATEVER about the WinSta0 object inside it - see E2. Opening the container confers no window access: reaching windows requires SetProcessWindowStation with a handle to the STATION, at WINSTA_* rights, which this does not obtain. E1 and E8 are unaffected by this row and rest on their own sentinels

assertions.title: open a desktop in another session window station (RETIRED — station-relative API, no route)
assertions.implies: NOTHING. The call is blocked parsing the name, so the desktop DACL is never consulted.
assertions.doesNotImply: in particular it does not imply that cross-session desktop access is denied. That remains NOT PROVEN in either direction until E3a reports.

assertions.title: open OUR OWN desktop by object-manager path (RETIRED — no route to a desktop leaf)
assertions.implies: the object-manager route can reach a desktop leaf at this mask for this token
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about another session; this is the control, not the measurement

assertions.title: open another session desktop by object-manager path (RETIRED — no route to a desktop leaf)
assertions.implies: NOTHING. The lookup never reaches a desktop object, so no DACL is ever consulted.
assertions.doesNotImply: above all it does not imply that cross-session desktop access is DENIED. Both routes were refused at the name, for our own session as well as the other one, so denial was never tested. Cross-session desktop access remains NOT PROVEN in either direction

assertions.title: read another session clipboard
assertions.postRunVerification: stage3-owner-clip.ps1 -Verify must re-read the OWNER clipboard AFTER the top-up and confirm the sentinel digest is unchanged. Until it does, a not-found is PENDING-VERIFY and may never be scored BOUNDED: the operator cannot tell containment from a sentinel that was overwritten, and finding out would require the very read E4 forbids
assertions.implies: the owner-seeded clipboard string is not obtainable from this session
assertions.doesNotImply: the clipboard is per-window-station, so a block at the window-station step is E2 mechanism reported again — it is NOT independent evidence about the clipboard object

assertions.title: open another session process for PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION
assertions.implies: OpenProcess succeeds only if ALL requested rights are granted, so denial of 0x0400 entails denial of any mask containing it, up to and including PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS
assertions.doesNotImply: NOTHING about PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION (0x1000). That is a separate, weaker right that can be granted independently, so no subset argument reaches it — see E6b

assertions.title: open another session process for PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
assertions.implies: denial of the weaker query right, which E6 could not reach
assertions.doesNotImply: a measurement in the louis to session-5 direction does not settle this. The directions are not symmetric and the ACLs need not be; this must be measured operator to owner

assertions.title: read another session process MainModule file name
assertions.implies: the module path of another session process is not readable by this account
assertions.doesNotImply: the process NAME and PID remain visible — that is E5, an accepted surface

assertions.title: capture another session screen
assertions.implies: a capture taken in this session does not contain the other session pixels
assertions.doesNotImply: it detects the owner SENTINEL COLOUR only. It cannot prove the absence of all owner-session content — only that the one marker made deliberately detectable is absent

assertions.title: read another session process command line
assertions.implies: command-line arguments of another session process are not readable by this account
assertions.doesNotImply: a null return from the query API alone names no mechanism and is INVALID; the row is only BOUNDED when the underlying OpenProcess denial is recorded with it

assertions.title: open another session process for PROCESS_TERMINATE
assertions.implies: the right to terminate is not held. The handle is requested and closed immediately; nothing is ever terminated
assertions.doesNotImply: this is NOT a replacement for E7. It was run under the E7 id once, which is the collision that produced this register

assertions.title: the own sentinel window appears in the own enumeration
assertions.implies: the enumerator is not blind, so E1 finding nothing means something
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about any other observation action

assertions.title: a capture of the own desktop contains the own sentinel colour
assertions.implies: the capture path works AND the sampled frame demonstrably holds the sentinel, so E8 finding no owner colour means something
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about UIA or window enumeration

assertions.title: the own sentinel window yields a NON-EMPTY automation tree
assertions.implies: the UIA reader is not blind — REQUIRES nodeCount > 0 and evidenceBytes > 0. A zero-node read is ACCEPTED by no rule; see the uia-zero-nodes vacuous-pass rule
assertions.doesNotImply: reading a window in this session says nothing about reading one in another

assertions.title: open the own session window-station container in the object manager
assertions.implies: the object-manager route works for this token at this mask, so E2 being refused is about the target and not about the call
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about desktops or the clipboard

assertions.title: open a desktop in the own window station
assertions.implies: OpenDesktop works for this token at this mask
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about another session window station

assertions.title: read a seeded string back from the own clipboard
assertions.implies: the clipboard reader works in this session, so E4 returning nothing means something
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about another window station clipboard

assertions.title: open an own-session process for PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION
assertions.implies: OpenProcess at THIS EXACT MASK succeeds in this session, which is what makes E6 a measurement of the target rather than of the mask
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about any other mask

assertions.title: open an own-session process for PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION
assertions.implies: OpenProcess at 0x1000 succeeds in this session
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about any other mask

assertions.title: open an own-session process for PROCESS_TERMINATE
assertions.implies: the handle is obtainable at 0x0001 in this session. It is CLOSED IMMEDIATELY and nothing is terminated, here or in E10
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about any other mask

assertions.title: read the own process MainModule file name
assertions.implies: the module reader works, so E7 returning nothing means something
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about another session

assertions.title: read the own process command line
assertions.implies: the query API returns a command line in this session, so a null for another session is a real difference rather than an API that never works
assertions.doesNotImply: nothing about the MECHANISM of that difference — E9 must record the OpenProcess denial to name one
